text:
If you’re stepping out for lunch or a walk, Burlington is delivering the pleasant version of Friday so far: clear skies, a cool 61, and a light west-northwest breeze. The sun should carry us into the low 70s this afternoon, with the lake staying friendly, north winds around 5 to 10 knots and waves a foot or less. Clouds build after sunset, but tonight looks dry, mostly cloudy, and cool, with temperatures sliding toward the low 50s.

Saturday is the less settled day. Expect a cloudy, breezy afternoon in the upper 60s, though the models disagree on how warm we get, and showers become more likely after 8 in the evening. The lake gets choppier too, with waves up to 3 feet and stronger north winds Saturday night. Enjoy the sunshine through late afternoon, keep tonight’s plans light, and don’t count on a smooth Saturday night on the water.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): After some morning fog, today will be mostly sunny in northern parts of our region. Southern sections will have more high clouds, actually due to the Nor’easter brewing off the Carolina coast. Highs will be in the low to mid-70s, making for a very pleasant day. For tonight, clouds will increase, and there’s the chance for showers in southern Vermont by daybreak. Models differ on how far north the showers get on Saturday. At this time, it’s expected to be cloudy in northern parts of the region with showers south. It will be breezy with a north wind 10 to 20 mph with possible higher gusts. The New England coast will be a different story with a storm warning in effect and wind gusts possibly over 60 mph. Highs on Saturday will be mainly in the 60s, though a few low 70s are possible north.
